# ADR 0006 — UUIDv7 primary keys generated by clients and server

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-26 · **Blueprint:** §6.3, §8.7 · **Database:** §2 · **Architecture:** §10 · **API:** §1

## Context
The Android field app creates surveys, photos, attendance and expense records offline and pushes them later, sometimes days later, through idempotent commands. Server-assigned sequential IDs would force a round trip before a record can be referenced, expose row counts to users, and make offline creation and retries ambiguous. Random UUIDv4 keys fragment B-tree indexes on tables that will hold tens of millions of rows.

## Decision
Every table uses an **`id uuid` primary key holding a UUIDv7**, generated by whoever creates the record: the server in commands, the field app for offline records.

- UUIDv7 keys are time-ordered, so inserts append to the index and keyset pagination by `(updated_at, id)` stays efficient.
- The field app generates the ID at creation, so a retried push is idempotent and photos and lines can reference their parent before the sync runs.
- Human-facing numbers (`quote_no`, `so_no`, `proforma_no`, `challan_no`) are separate business keys issued by `document_sequences` per entity, document type and financial year, gapless within a series. Primary keys are never shown to users or used in customer documents.
- `/api/v1` accepts and returns IDs as UUID strings; contracts validate them with Zod.
- One shared generator in `packages/contracts` is used by web, domain, field app and connector, so the format is identical everywhere.

## Consequences
- Offline-first sync (blueprint §8.7) works without ID reconciliation or temporary client IDs.
- Index locality is close to that of sequential integers while keys remain unguessable and globally unique across environments and imports.
- Clock skew on a device only affects ordering within the index, never uniqueness; the server's `created_at` remains the authoritative time.
- The `entities.id` column stays `smallint` because it is a fixed configuration table referenced from every business row; this is the one deliberate exception.
